title: Lubrication Technician
description:
The Lubrication Technician is responsible for executing Perry's world-class lubrication and asset care program to improve equipment reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, extend asset life, and lower maintenance costs. This position performs lubrication routes, oil sampling, contamination control activities, asset inspections, and lubrication PMs across production, packaging, utilities, refrigeration, and facility systems.

The Lubrication Technician serves as the facility subject matter expert for lubricant selection, lubrication best practices, contamination prevention, oil analysis, and equipment asset care. The role partners closely with the Reliability Engineer, PdM Technician, Maintenance Supervisors, and Asset Reliability Planner to support Perry's reliability strategy and TPM journey.

The primary purpose of this role is to:

  • Reduce lubrication-related equipment failures
  • Improve asset reliability
  • Increase equipment life expectancy
  • Prevent contamination-related failures
  • Improve PM effectiveness
  • Support planned maintenance activities
  • Increase uptime across critical processing and packaging asset

Key Responsibilities (Lubrication Program Execution)

  • Execute all scheduled lubrication routes and tasks.
  • Lubricate equipment according to approved lubrication standards.
  • Verify proper lubricant types and quantities.
  • Inspect lubrication points for proper function and condition.
  • Maintain lubrication frequencies and schedules.
  • Update lubrication records within the CMMS system.
  • Support shutdown lubrication activities.

Oil Sampling Program

  • Collect oil samples according to established schedules.
  • Prepare and submit samples for laboratory analysis.
  • Review oil analysis reports with the Reliability Engineer.
  • Identify contamination concerns.
  • Monitor lubricant condition and degradation trends.
  • Initiate work orders based on oil analysis findings.

Asset Condition Monitoring

Perform routine inspections of:

  • Bearings
  • Gearboxes
  • Motors
  • Chains
  • Couplings
  • Pumps
  • Hydraulic systems
  • Pneumatic systems

Document and communicate abnormal conditions including:

  • Leaks
  • Contamination
  • High temperatures
  • Excessive vibration
  • Lubricant degradation

Lubrication Storage & Inventory Management

Own and manage lubrication systems including:

  • Lubricant storage room
  • Bulk lubrication systems
  • Grease inventory
  • Oil inventory
  • Contamination control standards

Responsibilities include:

  • Proper storage practices
  • Labeling systems
  • Lubricant identification
  • Inventory rotation
  • Vendor coordination

Precision Lubrication

Support implementation of precision lubrication practices including:

  • Correct lubricant selection
  • Proper filtration techniques
  • Contamination prevention
  • Moisture control
  • Breather management
  • Lubricant handling procedures

Reliability Improvement Support

Partner with the Reliability Engineer to:

  • Analyze lubrication-related failures
  • Support Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA)
  • Develop lubrication PM standards
  • Improve Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF)
  • Reduce equipment downtime

TPM Support

Support TPM initiatives including:

  • Autonomous Maintenance development
  • Operator asset care training
  • Equipment basic conditions
  • Centerlining activities
  • Focused improvement projects

Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance

Maintain compliance with:

  • GMP requirements
  • HACCP requirements
  • USDA expectations
  • Plant sanitation policies
  • Food safety standards
  • Environmental regulations
  • Lockout/Tagout procedures

Ensure lubrication activities do not create product contamination risks.

Primary Assets Supported

Packaging Systems

  • Multivac thermoformers
  • Conveyors
  • Vacuum pumps
  • Case packers
  • Labeling equipment
  • Robotics

Processing Systems

  • Mixers
  • Grinders
  • Stuffers
  • Pumps
  • Conveyors

Utilities

  • Air compressors
  • Refrigeration compressors
  • Cooling tower equipment
  • Boilers
  • Water systems

Facility Assets

  • Motors
  • Gearboxes
  • Bearings
  • Fans
  • HVAC equipment
  • Material handling systems

Education

One of the following:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Technical School Certification
  • Industrial Maintenance Training

Experience

  • Minimum 3 years industrial maintenance experience
  • Experience performing lubrication routes preferred
  • Manufacturing experience required
  • Food manufacturing experience preferred

Preferred Certifications

  • Machinery Lubrication Technician (MLT I or II)
  • ICML Certification
  • Oil Analysis Certification
  • Certified Maintenance & Reliability Technician (CMRT)
  • Precision Lubrication Certification

Required Technical Skills

  • Industrial maintenance fundamentals
  • Lubrication practices
  • Mechanical systems knowledge
  • CMMS experience
  • Basic computer skills
  • Microsoft Excel

Preferred

  • Oil analysis interpretation
  • SAP PM
  • Fiix
  • Maintenance Connection
  • Reliability software
  • Precision lubrication practices

Success Measures - First 12 Months

First 90 Days

  • Complete lubrication route assessments.
  • Establish lubricant inventory controls.
  • Develop critical equipment lubrication maps.
  • Complete lubrication asset registry review.

First 6 Months

  • Achieve >95% route completion compliance.
  • Eliminate lubrication-related PM backlog.
  • Implement contamination control standards.
  • Expand oil sampling coverage of critical assets.

First 12 Months

  • Reduce lubrication-related equipment failures by 25%.
  • Improve bearing life on critical packaging assets.
  • Improve equipment uptime across packaging and utilities.
  • Support reduction of maintenance overtime from 12.9% toward <8%.
  • Contribute to Perry's reliability and TPM initiatives supporting 21MM+ annual pounds.

Why This Position Exists at Perry

Perry's 2027 growth plan requires increased equipment reliability, reduced maintenance overtime, improved PM effectiveness, and stronger asset care practices. Industry studies consistently show that poor lubrication practices are among the leading causes of rotating equipment failures.

The Lubrication Technician provides a dedicated reliability resource focused on precision lubrication, contamination control, and asset health preservation. This role supports Perry's transition from reactive maintenance to proactive reliability management and is expected to deliver measurable improvements in equipment uptime, maintenance costs, asset life, and overall plant performance.

The starting rate for this role is $29 - $34 (Hourly). Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, and candidate skill set and experience. While performing the duties of this job the Team Member will be required to wear the appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (i.e beard/hairnet, ear plugs, frock, boots, etc), stand for extended periods of time, and use hands/arms to push, pull, reach and occasionally lift above head. The Team Member must occasionally lift, push, pull up to 25 pounds and 50 pounds infrequently. Team Members are requested to visually inspect equipment and/or product.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. What Our Expectations Are:

In Commercial Support, we believe that everything starts with our people. We foster a learning organisation by providing opportunities for development, growth, and empowerment. We establish our products and services as the customer preferred choice by delivering world-class product & service dependability and benchmark customer service. We drive change and quality through our employee's imagination, dedication, and skills of their craft. We augment this by using technology, striving for proactivity, synergy, and always acting with integrity and respect. The P&WC Commercial Support organization supports a multidisciplinary eco-system.

Functional Description:

The Claims Adjudicator is responsible for the timely, accurate, and consistent review, analysis, and adjudication of Pratt & Whitney warranty claims. This role ensures claims are assessed in accordance with applicable warranty policies, Power-by-the-Hour (PPH) program contracts, commercial agreements, and technical publications. The Claims Adjudicator plays a critical role in protecting the integrity of warranty programs while ensuring customers receive fair and compliant claim settlements.

Success in this position requires strong analytical abilities, exceptional attention to detail, the capability to interpret complex technical documentation, and a solid understanding of commercial warranty offerings and contractual obligations.

What You Will Do:

  • Warranty Claim Review & Adjudication
  • Review and adjudicate warranty claims in accordance with company warranty policies, PPH program contracts, commercial agreements, and applicable procedures.
  • Evaluate claim documentation, maintenance records, invoices, and supporting evidence to determine warranty eligibility and claim validity.
  • Verify claim compliance with contractual obligations, warranty coverage, technical requirements, and customer agreements.
  • Calculate and authorize accurate claim settlements while ensuring financial accuracy and consistency.
  • Document claim decisions clearly and maintain complete records to support audit requirements and future reference.
  • Ensures KPIs are adhered to.
  • Technical Analysis & Compliance
  • Interpret and apply technical publications including maintenance manuals, service bulletins, engineering documentation, component manuals, and other OEM technical references.
  • Assess technical findings and maintenance actions to determine whether repairs or replacements meet warranty requirements.
  • Commercial & Contract Interpretation
  • Interpret and apply commercial warranty terms, PPH contracts, customer-specific agreements, and service offerings during claim evaluation.
  • Identify contractual inconsistencies or areas requiring clarification and escalate as appropriate.
  • Investigation & Trend Analysis
  • Support the investigation of claim discrepancies, unusual claim activity, and recurring issues to determine underlying causes.
  • Support the identification of trends in warranty claims that may indicate product reliability concerns, process deficiencies, customer maintenance practices, or commercial risks.
  • Escalate significant technical, financial, or operational findings to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration
  • Work closely with internal and external stakeholders as required to resolve claim issues.
  • Communicate claim decisions clearly and professionally and provide technical or contractual justification when required.
  • Support internal and external audits by providing accurate documentation and claim rationale.
  • Contribute to a collaborative environment focused on delivering consistent and equitable claim outcomes.
  • Continuous Improvement/ Compliance
  • Recommend improvements to warranty policies, adjudication processes, documentation, and commercial practices.
  • Support initiatives that improve claim accuracy, automation, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction.
  • Stay current on changes to warranty policies, PPH contracts, technical publications, commercial offerings, and industry best practices.
  • Participate in training and knowledge-sharing activities to promote consistent adjudication standards.
  • Comply with the EH&S Policy and applicable regulatory and company EH&S rules and requirements.
  • Comply with Global Trade requirements (export controls).

Required Skills:

Customer Service Excellence: Ability to provide outstanding service and resolve complex customer issues with a customer-first mindset.
Understanding of Aerospace service ecosystem: Customer services, aftermarket, MRO, warranty, contracts, etc.


Technical/Commercial Knowledge: Ability to interpret technical publications, engineering documentation, and contractual language.


Problem-Solving: Analytical and resourceful approach to diagnose problems and identifying effective solutions.


Communication Skills: Excellent English verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical customers.


Organizational Skills: Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple claims and priorities simultaneously.


Resilience and Persistence: Ability to follow through on complex issues and ensure resolution to completion with a medium degree of autonomy.


Qualifications You Must Have:

  • Related field are Business Administration, Aerospace, Engineering or the like.

Heavy Equipment Operator (GPS Machine Control) | $40/hr + LOA | Slave Lake, AB
Slave Lake, Alberta | Full-Time
Heavy Equipment Operation / Earthworks | Experienced | Day Shift
Hiring now. Qualified operators are being interviewed this week.
GrizzlyTrek is hiring GPS machine control operators out of Slave Lake for civil earthworks, lease construction and access roads. The rate is $40.00 an hour with a Living Out Allowance on top, full time, with work booked through the season. GPS experience is a hard requirement on this one, not an asset.

Pay$40.00 per hour
Living Out AllowanceLOA provided
Position TypeFull-Time
LocationSlave Lake, Alberta and surrounding area
ScheduleDay shift, 10 to 12 hour days, six days a week through the season
OvertimeAvailable based on operational requirements
EquipmentDozer, excavator or grader running GPS machine control
ExperienceVerifiable GPS machine control seat time. This one is a must have.
CertificationClass 5 licence, CSTS or equivalent, Ground Disturbance, H2S Alive, First Aid
ResidencyOpen to operators who will travel, with LOA provided
StartImmediate
The Work
Work runs out of Slave Lake and across the Lesser Slave Lake region. It is civil earthworks and site prep close in, and lease construction, access roads and reclamation out of town: stripping topsoil, cut and fill, building pads, roads and parking areas, and holding grade to the model. The machines are set up on GPS, so you are building to a design file rather than a stack of stakes, and you are expected to catch a bad model before you build off it.
What You'll Do
  • Run dozer, excavator or grader on GPS machine control, building to the design model
  • Load the model, run a localization and benchmark check, and hold grade through the shift
  • Strip topsoil, move cut and fill, and build pads, roads and parking areas to grade
  • Dig, slope and backfill trench for underground utilities and pipe
  • Flag model, base station or rover problems early rather than building off a bad file
  • Complete daily walkarounds, pre-trip inspections and greasing before the machine moves
  • Take part in pre-job safety meetings, hazard assessments and toolbox talks
What You Bring
  • Verifiable GPS machine control seat time on dozer, excavator or grader (Trimble, Topcon or Leica)
  • Able to load a model, run a localization check and hold grade without a grade checker on you
  • Seat time in civil earthworks, lease construction or forestry construction
  • Valid Class 5 licence and reliable transportation to site
  • Common site tickets: CSTS or equivalent, Ground Disturbance, H2S Alive and First Aid
  • Able to pass a pre-employment drug and alcohol test and work outdoors through the season
Nice to Have
  • Time on more than one GPS platform (Trimble, Topcon or Leica)
  • A second and third seat: dozer, excavator, grader or loader
  • Class 1 or Class 3 licence for equipment moves and float work
Why Operators Take This Job
The rate is posted at $40.00 with LOA on top, and it is not talked down after the interview, because running GPS is exactly what you are being paid for. The work is booked through the season, so you are not running one job for three weeks and then calling around again. Operators who can actually run a model get the grade work here instead of being handed a machine and a stack of stakes.
Pay is a gross hourly rate before deductions.
What We Offer
  • $40.00 per hour, plus Living Out Allowance
  • Overtime available based on operational requirements
  • Life insurance plus AD&D with critical illness and cancer coverage
  • Extended health: drugs, hospital, vision, and paramedical including mental health
  • Dental coverage, including orthodontic coverage for children
  • Travel insurance, plus ongoing training and career development support
About GrizzlyTrek
GrizzlyTrek Group is a Technical Workforce and Indigenous Employment Partner. We recruit skilled trades across Canada's industrial sector and place them with reputable employers offering long term work, fair pay, and room to advance. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and proudly support Indigenous employment.

Run GPS machine control and want a full season of grade work with LOA? Apply today at www.grizzlytrekgroup.com. Qualified candidates will be contacted quickly.

title: Global ERP Program Director
description:
Global ERP Program Director – 18 month to 2 year fixed-term contract

Join us and be part of a mission-driven, independent publisher. You’ll work with a diverse group of people who share a passion for empowering researchers, educators, and institutions to shape the future.

About Sage:

Sage is a global academic publisher of books, journals, and library resources with a growing range of technologies to enable discovery, access, and engagement. Believing that research and education are critical in shaping society, Sara Miller McCune founded Sage in 1965. Today, we are controlled by a group of trustees charged with maintaining our independence and mission indefinitely.

Our guaranteed independence means we’re free to:

  • Do more – supporting an equitable academic future, furthering disciplines that drive social change, and helping social and behavioural science make an impact

  • Work together – building lasting relationships, championing diverse perspectives, and co-creating resources to transform teaching and learning

  • Think long-term – experimenting, taking risks, and investing in new ideas

About our Team:

The Global Finance team at Sage is a collaborative, high‑performing function with finance teams and business leaders across the US, UK and India. Together, we support Sage’s growth by delivering trusted financial insights, strong governance and modern, scalable processes. As we embark on a multi‑year transformation to create a single global finance system, this team will play a pivotal role in shaping how Sage operates, ensuring our colleagues have consistent, reliable and intuitive tools that enable confident decision‑making and seamless global collaboration.

Could you be our new ERP Program Director? Are you?

  • Experienced in leading large‑scale ERP transformations across multiple regions, with a track record of delivering measurable business outcomes?

  • Confident influencing C‑suite and board‑level stakeholders, building trust through sound judgement, integrity and consistent delivery?

  • Skilled at driving global process harmonisation, balancing simplification with regulatory and financial control requirements?

  • Able to lead high‑performing cross‑functional teams, strengthening collaboration and reducing organisational friction?

  • Experienced in programme governance, risk management, financial control and vendor oversight for programmes exceeding $20m?

  • Knowledgeable about modern ERP platforms, cloud‑based architectures, integrations, data migration and multi‑phase delivery?

  • An exceptional communicator who can translate complex concepts clearly for both technical and non‑technical audiences?

  • Passionate about organisational change, ensuring colleagues are supported through training, communication and adoption planning?

Your new role:

The Global ERP Program Director is a senior, business‑critical leader responsible for delivering one of Sage’s most important global transformation programmes. Reporting to the CFO and working in close partnership with the CIO, you will lead the design, delivery and adoption of a single, cloud‑based ERP system that modernises our operating platform, simplifies global processes and creates a trusted financial system of record. You will bring clarity, momentum and strategic alignment across regions, ensuring the programme delivers measurable business outcomes and sets the foundation for Sage’s next phase of growth.

  • Deliver a single global ERP instance that provides a trusted financial system with consistent, high‑quality data.

  • Establish and embed a global programme governance model that enables fast, transparent decision‑making and strong executive alignment.

  • Create and maintain an integrated programme plan covering design, build, testing, data, integrations, change and deployment across all regions.

  • Drive global process standardisation using “global first, local by exception” principles, ensuring compliance while reducing complexity.

  • Lead organisational change and adoption activities, ensuring colleagues are ready, supported and confident ahead of go‑live.

  • Manage systems integrators and external partners, holding them accountable for delivery quality, milestones and knowledge transfer.

  • Ensure risks, issues and dependencies are proactively managed, escalated and resolved to keep the programme on track.

Overview of benefits:

  • 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) with 2 additional floating personal days.

  • Hybrid working up to 2 days per week in office and a home working allowance.

  • Life assurance, income protection, and travel insurance.

  • Private medical cover and access to the company doctor.

  • Tuition scheme and support for pursuing professional qualifications, including access to Sage books and journals.

  • Variety of snacks and beverages available in the office.

  • Healthy lifestyle reimbursement and anniversary trips.

  • Access to Company loans (season ticket loan, rental deposit loan, cycle loan).

We’re a Disability Confident Employer (Level 1). If you’d like to apply under this scheme, please let us know in your application.

We’re committed to making our recruitment process accessible and inclusive. If you’d like to request reasonable adjustments, please email humanresources@sagepub.co.uk. Please note we only accept applications via email if an adjustment has been agreed.

At Sage, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and to sustaining a culture that celebrates diversity, encourages authenticity, and builds a deep sense of belonging. title: Data Scientist
description:
Foxway seeks Data Scientist for Pricing & Business Modelling

About the Role

Join a leading European company in the technology refurbishing sector as a Data Scientist. You will work on real operational problems involving pricing, inventory and demand modelling, optimization and decision-support tools. The role spans the full data science lifecycle — from understanding the business problem and developing models to production deployment, monitoring and continuous improvement.
This is a great opportunity to take meaningful ownership early and work at the intersection of data science, commercial decision-making and operational complexity.


Key Responsibilities

Algorithm Development & Automation

  • Design, build, and implement machine learning and statistical models to automate pricing and business decisions for refurbished mobile devices, from prototype to production environment

  • Develop robust, scalable modelling solutions that address real-world pricing and business challenges, including dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, competitor analysis, and other business modelling use cases

  • Explore and evaluate new modelling approaches and data sources to improve decision quality.

Business Insight & Model Translation

  • Collaborate closely with business, operations, and product stakeholders to distil complex requirements into actionable data science solutions

  • Translate operational and market insights into predictive and statistical models that drive measurable business value

  • Support business modelling initiatives beyond pricing, such as demand planning, inventory optimization, or customer analytics, as our data science scope expands

Model Development & Continuous Improvement

  • Continuously monitor model performance and business outcome, address issues such as data drift or model degradation, and retrain models as necessary to maintain optimal accuracy

  • Develop appropriate validation and experimentation approaches to evaluate models and decision strategies.

  • Build analytical and monitoring solutions that make model behaviour and business impact transparent. Stay current with the latest research and industry best practices, supporting the implementation of new approaches to improve pricing outcomes

Collaboration & Communication

  • Work cross-functionally with engineering, data, and business teams to ensure seamless integration of pricing models into business systems

  • Help ensure deployed solutions are reliable, maintainable and appropriately monitored.

  • Communicate analytical findings, model behaviour, uncertainty and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, enabling data-driven decision making.

Required Qualifications

  • 2-5 years of hands-on experience in Data Science, Machine Learning or a closely related applied modelling role. Experience with designing and maintaining life cycle of machine learning models in production is required.

  • Proficiency in Python and SQL; experience with common ML libraries (e.g., scikit-learn, LightGBM or XGBoost).

  • Solid understanding of statistical analysis, predictive modelling, model validation and feature engineering.

  • Experience developing and maintaining models or analytical solutions beyond the initial prototype stage. Ability to translate ambiguous business and operational problems into quantitative solutions.

  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills and an interest in understanding how models behave in real operational environments. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present complex results clearly and persuasively

  • Degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in pricing, e-commerce, marketplaces, retail, recommerce or another data-intensive commercial environment.

  • Experience with pricing optimization, price elasticity, demand forecasting, inventory modelling or revenue management.

  • Experience with model monitoring, automated ML pipelines or production ML systems.

  • Familiar with cloud environments such as AWS, GCP or Azure and containerization such as Docker.

  • Interest or experience in modern AI/LLM applications where relevant to business problems.

Help us make a difference!

We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so if this sounds like the next step in your career, apply quickly!

How does Foxway operate?

Foxway is a fast-growing and dynamic organization with an international team of nearly 1,300 people, including close to 600 colleagues in Estonia. We operate across multiple countries, with key hubs across Europe.

Our mission is to make sustainable technology accessible to everyone. Through Foxway Recommerce Mobiles, we give smart devices a second life, helping to reduce environmental impact and support a more circular future.

By joining us, you become part of a purpose-driven, international team that is shaping the future of sustainable workplaces and circular technology.

title: Data QA Engineer
description:
About ClearGrid

ClearGrid is revolutionizing the debt resolution industry with cutting-edge AI and advanced analytics. We leverage real-time data, machine learning, and automation to optimize debt recovery for financial institutions. As we scale our technology platform, we are building high-performance, resilient systems to support our next phase of hyper-growth.

Why this role exists

ClearGrid runs collections journeys across AI voice, human agents, SMS, WhatsApp and email for lenders in the UAE and KSA. Every decision — who we call, when we call them, what a promise-to-pay is worth, what we invoice a client — sits on top of data that moves from MongoDB and telephony providers into BigQuery, through dbt, and out into Tableau dashboards, Streamlit apps and client-facing reports. When that data is wrong, the consequences are not cosmetic: we call a borrower who has already paid, we mis-state a lender's recovery rate in a QBR, or we bill against the wrong call window. This role exists to stop that happening — and to catch it fast when it does.

What you'll own

• Test coverage in dbt across staging, intermediate and mart layers — not just not_null and unique, but business-rule tests that encode how collections actually works (DPD bucket transitions, PTP date logic, disposition hierarchies, currency and amount sanity checks).

• Source-to-warehouse reconciliation between MongoDB, telephony systems, client files and BigQuery: row counts, per-lender counts, per-lender-per-DPD-bucket counts, and orphan/drift detection.

• Freshness, volume and schema-drift monitoring on critical tables, with clear ownership of what "broken" means for each.

• Inbound client file QA — validating lender account files (fields, formats, phone numbers, names, dates, encodings) before they ever reach a journey.

• Report and dashboard QA — every Tableau dashboard and client report gets checked before it ships. Do the headline numbers reconcile to the warehouse? Do the filters, date ranges and parameters change the figures the way they should? Do totals hold when you slice by lender, by campaign, by DPD bucket? Are nulls being silently dropped from a denominator? Does the same metric agree across two dashboards that both claim to show it?

• Pre-release QA of new dbt models and metric definitions before anything downstream is built on them.

• The data incident process — detection, triage, stakeholder comms, root cause, and the fix that stops

the repeat.

What we're looking for

Must Haves:

• 2+ years in data quality, analytics engineering, BI QA, or a data analyst role with heavy quality ownership.

• Strong SQL — CTEs, window functions, incremental patterns, and awareness of query cost. BigQuery/GoogleSQL preferred; any warehouse dialect considered.

• Python for validation scripts and automation (pandas or equivalent).

• Git-based workflow: branches, PRs, code review.

• An investigative temperament. You are not satisfied by "the numbers changed" — you want to know

which record, which join, which timezone.

• Clear written communication. Much of the job is explaining a data problem to someone who doesn't

want to hear about it.

Nice to have

• Collections, lending, or fintech domain knowledge — DPD buckets, roll rates, PTP, recovery rate, settlement.

• Prefect (or Airflow) orchestration.

• MongoDB and semi-structured/JSON data handling.

• Streamlit, or any BI tool (Tableau, Power BI, Looker) — as a user, not necessarily a builder.

• Data quality frameworks: dbt-expectations, Elementary, Great Expectations, or similar.

  • Participate in an Integrated Product Team to design new capabilities based upon evaluation of all necessary development and operational considerations
  • Allocate real-time process budgets and error budgets to systems and subsystem components
  • Generate alternative system concepts, physical architectures, and design solutions
  • Define the methods, processes, and evaluation criteria by which the systems, subsystems and work products are verified against their requirements in a written plan
  • Develop system design solution that satisfies the system requirements and fulfills the functional analysis
  • Review and provide input to program and contract work breakdown structure (WBS), work packages and the integrated master plan (IMP)
  • Participate in the development of system engineering documentation, such as System Engineering Plans, Initial Capabilities Documents, Requirements Specifications, and Interface Control Documents
  • Participate in interface definition, design, and changes to the configuration between affected groups and individuals throughout the life cycle
  • Derive from the system requirements an understanding of stakeholder needs, functions that may be logically inferred and implied as essential to system effectiveness
  • Derive lower-level requirements from higher-level allocated requirements that describe in detail the functions that a system component must fulfill, and ensure these requirements are complete, correct, unique, unambiguous, realizable, and verifiable
  • Participate in establishing and gaining approval of the definition of a system or component under development (requirements, designs, interfaces, test procedures, etc.) that provides a common reference point for hardware and software developers
  • Develop derived requirements for Information Assurance Services (Confidentiality, Integrity, Non repudiation, and Availability); Basic Information Assurance Mechanisms (e.g., Identification, Authentication, Access Control, Accountability); and Security Mechanism Technology (Passwords, cryptography, discretionary access control, mandatory access control, hashing, key management, etc.)
  • Implement comprehensive SOA solutions
  • Implement operational view, technical standards view, and system and services view for Architectures using applicable DoDAF standards
  • Review and/or approve system engineering documentation to ensure that processes and specifications meet system needs and are accurate, comprehensive, and complete
  • Capture all interface designs in a common interface control format, and store interface data in a commonly accessible repository
  • Assess each risk to the program and determine the probability of occurrence and quantified
  • Consequence of failure in accordance with an approved risk management plan
  • In conjunction with system stakeholders, plan the verification efforts of new and unproven designs early in the development life cycle to ensure compliance with established requirements
  • Prepare time-line analysis diagrams illustrating the flow of time-dependent functions
  • Establish a process to formally and proactively control and manage changes to requirements, consider impacts prior to commitment to change, gain stakeholder buy-in, eliminate ambiguity, ensure traceability to source requirements, and track and settle open actions
  • Manage and ensure the technical integrity of the system baseline over time, continually updating it as various changes are imposed on the system during the lifecycle from development through deployment and operations & maintenance
  • Support the planning and test analysis of the DoD Certification/Accreditation Process (as well as other Government Certification and Accreditation (C&A) processes support the development and review of Joint Capability Integration Development System (JCIDS) documents (i.e., Initial Capability Document, Capabilities Description Document, IA Strategy)
  • Provide technical direction for the development, engineering, interfacing, integration, and Testing of specific components of complex hardware/software systems to include requirements elicitation, analysis and functional allocation, conducting systems requirements reviews, developing concepts of operation and interface standards, developing system architectures, and performing technical/non-technical assessment and management as well as end-to-end flow analysis
  • Develop scenarios (threads) and an Operational Concept that describes the interactions between the system, the user, and the environment, that satisfies operational, support, maintenance, and disposal needs
  • Conduct quantitative analysis in non-functional system performance areas like Reliability, Maintainability, Vulnerability, Survivability, Producibility, etc.)
  • Establish and follow a formal procedure for coordinating system integration activities among multiple teams, ensuring complete coverage of all interfaces

What You Bring

  • Experience supporting government or DoD programs
  • Ability to work independently and within a collaborative team environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Fourteen (14) years experience as a SE in programs and contracts of similar scope, type and complexity are required. Bachelor's degree in System Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering Science, Engineering Management, or related discipline from an accredited college or university is required. Five (5) years of additional SE experience may be substituted for a bachelor's degree.

Preferred Qualifications

Titre du poste : Coordonnateur(trice) de programme - Expérience employé et cycle de vie des compétences

À propos de & Whitney Canada

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix

Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe ?

En tant que coordonnateur(trice) – Expérience employé et cycle de vie des compétences, vous soutenez la coordination, la mise en œuvre et l’amélioration continue des initiatives liées à l’expérience employé et au développement des compétences au sein des Opérations globales, avec un accent initial et prioritaire sur l’accueil et l’intégration des nouveaux employés.

En collaboration étroite avec les gestionnaires, les Ressources humaines, les experts de contenu, les partenaires en apprentissage et développement ainsi que les représentants de l’entreprise, vous veillez à ce que les nouveaux employés bénéficient d’une expérience d’intégration structurée, cohérente et adaptée à leur rôle.

Vous agissez comme point de coordination central pour les horaires d’intégration, les communications, les activités d’apprentissage, les suivis auprès des parties prenantes, la documentation, la rétroaction des employés et le suivi des progrès. Vous contribuez également à assurer le lien entre l’intégration, la préparation à l’emploi, le développement des compétences et le parcours global de l’employé.

Grâce à votre travail, vous contribuez à améliorer l’intégration des employés, la clarté de leur rôle, leur délai d’atteinte de l’autonomie et, plus largement, leur expérience au cours de leurs premières semaines et de leurs premiers mois au sein de l’organisation.

Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien ?

Coordination du programme d’intégration

  • Coordonner l’exécution de bout en bout du programme d’intégration des Opérations globales.
  • Maintenir les calendriers, échéanciers, listes de contrôle, modèles et plans de mise en œuvre liés à l’intégration.
  • Coordonner les activités d’intégration, de la préintégration jusqu’aux 30, 60 et 90 premiers jours de l’employé.
  • Veiller à ce que les activités d’intégration, les rencontres et les séances d’apprentissage requises soient planifiées et complétées.
  • Coordonner les séances d’orientation, les présentations des opérations, les formations techniques et les activités de développement propres au rôle.
  • Organiser les cohortes d’intégration et maintenir des listes de participants exactes.
  • Coordonner les animateurs, présentateurs, experts de contenu et ressources d’apprentissage.
  • Effectuer les suivis auprès des gestionnaires et des parties prenantes concernant les actions, informations et livrables en attente.
  • Identifier les conflits d’horaire, les risques liés à l’exécution et les contraintes de ressources, et faire remonter les enjeux au besoin.
  • Maintenir une documentation d’intégration exacte, accessible et à jour.

Soutien aux employés et aux gestionnaires

  • Agir comme point de contact central pour les questions liées à l’intégration provenant des employés, des gestionnaires et des partenaires d’affaires.

  • Fournir aux gestionnaires les plans d’intégration, listes de contrôle, modèles et outils de soutien.

  • Communiquer les attentes, responsabilités et échéanciers liés à l’intégration.

  • Soutenir les gestionnaires dans l’adaptation du cadre commun d’intégration au rôle, à la discipline, à l’unité d’affaires et au lieu de travail de l’employé.

  • Aider les employés à naviguer parmi les ressources d’apprentissage, les systèmes, l’information organisationnelle et les possibilités de développement disponibles.

  • Suivre la progression de l’intégration et coordonner les suivis lorsque certaines activités sont retardées ou incomplètes.

  • Favoriser une expérience employé accueillante, structurée et cohérente.

Coordination de l’apprentissage et du développement des compétences

  • Coordonner les activités d’apprentissage liées aux rôles avec les gestionnaires, les experts de contenu et les partenaires en apprentissage.

  • Soutenir le développement et la mise à jour des parcours d’intégration selon le rôle, la discipline et la population d’employés.

  • Faire le lien entre les exigences d’intégration, les responsabilités du poste, les profils de compétences et les parcours de développement des capacités.

  • Coordonner les activités d’apprentissage techniques, opérationnelles, de conformité et organisationnelles requises.

  • Intégrer la formation en cours d’emploi, l’accompagnement, le mentorat et l’observation en milieu de travail aux plans d’intégration.

  • Effectuer le suivi de la réalisation des activités d’apprentissage et de développement requises.

  • Identifier les écarts récurrents en matière de compétences et communiquer les constats aux responsables de programmes concernés.

Coordination des parties prenantes

  • Établir des relations de travail efficaces avec les Ressources humaines, les gestionnaires responsables de l’embauche, les leaders d’affaires, les équipes d’apprentissage et développement, les experts de contenu et les fonctions de soutien.

  • Coordonner les activités d’intégration entre les différentes unités d’affaires, les sites et les régions des Opérations globales.

  • Faciliter les rencontres de planification et de suivi de l’intégration.

  • Préparer les ordres du jour, documenter les décisions et assurer le suivi des actions jusqu’à leur réalisation.

  • Clarifier les rôles et responsabilités des parties prenantes.

  • Soutenir la mise en œuvre des normes communes des Opérations globales tout en tenant compte des exigences locales et régionales.

  • Maintenir un réseau actif de contacts et de contributeurs en matière d’intégration.

Expérience employé et rétroaction

  • Recueillir les commentaires des nouveaux employés, des gestionnaires et des personnes contribuant au processus d’intégration.

  • Coordonner les sondages d’intégration et les suivis structurés à des moments clés, notamment au cours de la première semaine et aux étapes des 30, 60 et 90 jours.

  • Identifier les expériences positives, les irritants récurrents et les possibilités d’amélioration.

  • Soutenir l’analyse de la rétroaction des employés et des résultats liés à l’intégration.

  • Contribuer à transformer les commentaires et les constats en améliorations concrètes du programme.

  • Favoriser la prise en compte de la voix des employés tout au long de leur expérience d’intégration.

  • Veiller à la cohérence et à la qualité de l’expérience employé entre les différents sites et les différentes populations d’employés.

Rapports et mesure de la performance

  • Maintenir des dossiers d’intégration, des informations sur les participants et une documentation de programme exacts.

  • Élaborer et mettre à jour les tableaux de bord, rapports d’état et indicateurs de performance liés à l’intégration.

  • Suivre des indicateurs

  • Préparer des mises à jour régulières du programme couvrant les réalisations, les prochaines étapes, les défis, les risques et les possibilités d’amélioration.

  • Identifier les tendances et recommander des améliorations à l’exécution du programme et aux résultats liés à l’expérience employé.

  • Protéger les renseignements personnels des employés et maintenir un niveau de confidentialité approprié.

Amélioration continue

  • Soutenir l’amélioration continue de la méthodologie, du contenu et des outils d’intégration des Opérations globales.

  • Examiner la rétroaction, les données de performance et les leçons apprises.

  • Comparer les pratiques d’intégration et d’expérience employé aux meilleures pratiques du marché.

  • Contribuer à standardiser et à simplifier les processus d’intégration au sein des Opérations globales.

  • Soutenir le développement et la mise à l’essai de nouveaux modèles, outils et solutions numériques.

  • Coordonner la mise à jour des documents d’intégration avec les responsables de contenu et les experts de contenu.

  • Documenter les processus et les méthodes de travail standard afin d’améliorer la cohérence et la pérennité du programme.

Soutien au programme du cycle de vie de l’employé

  • Soutenir certaines initiatives liées à l’ensemble du cycle de vie de l’expérience employé et du développement des compétences, selon l’évolution des priorités.

  • Contribuer à établir des liens entre l’intégration et le développement, la gestion de la performance, l’évolution de carrière, la mobilité interne, le transfert des connaissances et la relève.

  • Maintenir la documentation, les cartographies de processus, les outils et les suivis liés au cycle de vie de l’employé.

  • Soutenir les activités de consultation et d’écoute des employés à des moments clés de leur parcours.

  • Coordonner les actions interfonctionnelles découlant des constats liés à l’expérience employé.

  • Contribuer au développement d’une expérience employé intégrée et cohérente au sein des Opérations globales.

Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir ?

  • Diplôme de baccalauréat en ressources humaines, développement organisationnel, administration des affaires, éducation, communications, gestion de projets ou dans un domaine connexe; ou combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience pertinente.

  • Environ trois à cinq ans d’expérience en coordination de programmes, intégration des employés, expérience employé, apprentissage et développement, ressources humaines ou coordination de projets.

  • Expérience démontrée dans la coordination de plusieurs activités, échéanciers, parties prenantes et livrables.

  • Excellentes compétences en organisation, en planification et en suivi.

  • Excellentes compétences en communication, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.

  • Capacité à travailler efficacement avec des employés, des gestionnaires et des leaders à différents niveaux de l’organisation.

  • Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités dans un environnement complexe et en constante évolution.

  • Maîtrise de Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook et Teams.

  • Expérience dans la tenue de dossiers de programmes, de suivis, de tableaux de bord ou de rapports d’état.

Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.

Ce que nous offrons

  • Programme de régime de retraite et d’épargne avec cotisation de l’employeur

  • Programme d’assurance collective

  • Possibilités d’avancement (progression de carrière)

  • Programme de mérite ou programme de reconnaissance

  • Programme de santé et bien-être, y compris la télémédecine

  • Club récréatif et sportif

  • Garderies à proximité

  • Accessibilité en transport ou programme de transport en commun et stationnement gratuit

Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada

Le masculin est utilisé sans discrimination et uniquement dans le but d’alléger le texte. Nous étudierons la demande d’emploi de tous les candidats qualifiés.

Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, nous allions avec passion, audace et rigueur pour concevoir, fabriquer et entretenir les moteurs d’aéronefs les plus avancés et les plus fiables au monde. Notre travail et la qualité de nos produits contribuent au succès de nos clients, qui à leur tour sauvent des vies, soutiennent le commerce, connectent les communautés et protègent les libertés.

Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, vous avez l’occasion de faire une différence tous les jours ; il suffit de lever les yeux. Êtes-vous prêt à vous dépasser ?

Job title : Employee Experience & Capability Life Cycle – Program Coordinator

About Pratt & Whitney Canada

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) is a global leader in aerospace innovation, proudly headquartered in Longueuil, Quebec, since 1928. We design and manufacture next-generation aircraft engines that power the world’s largest fleet of business, general aviation, and regional aircraft and helicopters.

For nearly 100 years, our teams have been at the forefront of propulsion technology, pushing boundaries to make flight more efficient and reliable. Our engines support missions that truly matter, from transporting people and essential goods, to enabling emergency medical services, humanitarian operations, and wildfire suppression around the world.

An Employer of Choice

Pratt & Whitney Canada was named one of Canada’s Best Employers for 2026 by Forbes, marking the 11th consecutive year the company has earned this recognition. Pratt & Whitney Canada also ranked #1 employer in the aerospace and defense industry in the country. In addition, our headquarters continues to be recognized among the top employers in the Montreal region. Together, these distinctions reinforce our reputation as an employer of choice in Montreal, across Canada, and around the world.

Why join our team?

As the Employee Experience & Capability Life Cycle – Program Coordinator, you support the coordination, implementation and continuous improvement of employee experience and capability-development initiatives across Global Operations, with an initial and primary focus on the onboarding and integration stage.

Working closely with managers, Human Resources, subject-matter experts, Learning and Development partners and business representatives, you ensure that new employees receive a structured, consistent and role-relevant onboarding experience.

You serve as a central point of coordination for onboarding schedules, communications, learning activities, stakeholder follow-ups, documentation, employee feedback and progress tracking. You also support the connection between onboarding, role readiness, capability development and the broader employee life cycle.

Through your work, you contribute to improving employee integration, role clarity, time to proficiency and the overall employee experience during the first days and months of employment.

The position is based at our Longueuil location, from Monday to Friday, with flexible hours and exclusively on-site.

What will your day-to-day look like?

Onboarding Program Coordination

  • Coordinate the end-to-end execution of the Global Operations onboarding program.
  • Maintain onboarding schedules, calendars, checklists, templates and implementation plans.
  • Coordinate onboarding activities from pre-boarding through the employee’s first 30, 60 and 90 days.
  • Ensure that required onboarding activities, meetings and learning sessions are scheduled and completed.
  • Coordinate orientation sessions, operational overviews, technical training and role-specific development activities.
  • Organize onboarding cohorts and maintain accurate participant lists.
  • Coordinate facilitators, presenters, subject-matter experts and learning resources.
  • Follow up with managers and stakeholders regarding outstanding actions, information and deliverables.
  • Identify scheduling conflicts, execution risks and resource constraints, escalating issues when necessary.
  • Maintain accurate, accessible and current onboarding documentation.


Employee and Manager Support

  • Serve as a central point of contact for onboarding-related questions from employees, managers and business partners.
  • Provide managers with onboarding plans, checklists, templates and supporting tools.
  • Communicate onboarding expectations, responsibilities and timelines.
  • Support managers in adapting the common onboarding framework to the employee’s role, discipline, business unit and location.
  • Help employees navigate available learning resources, systems, organizational information and development opportunities.
  • Monitor onboarding progress and coordinate follow-up when activities are delayed or incomplete.
  • Promote a welcoming, structured and consistent employee experience.


Learning and Capability Coordination

  • Coordinate role-based learning activities with managers, subject-matter experts and learning partners.
  • Support the development and maintenance of onboarding curricula by role, discipline and employee population.
  • Connect onboarding requirements with job responsibilities, competency profiles and capability-development pathways.
  • Coordinate required technical, operational, compliance and organizational learning activities.
  • Integrate on-the-job training, coaching, mentoring and job-shadowing activities into onboarding plans.
  • Track the completion of required learning and development activities.
  • Identify recurring capability gaps and communicate findings to the appropriate program owners.


Stakeholder Coordination

  • Build effective working relationships with Human Resources, hiring managers, business leaders, Learning and Development teams, subject-matter experts and support functions.
  • Coordinate onboarding activities across Global Operations business units, sites and regions.
  • Facilitate onboarding planning and progress-review meetings.
  • Prepare meeting agendas, document decisions and track actions through completion.
  • Clarify stakeholder roles and responsibilities.
  • Support the implementation of common Global Operations standards while recognizing local and regional requirements.
  • Maintain an active network of onboarding contacts and contributors.


Employee Experience and Feedback

  • Collect feedback from new employees, managers and onboarding contributors.
  • Coordinate onboarding surveys and structured check-ins at key moments, including the first week and the 30-, 60- and 90-day milestones.
  • Identify positive experiences, recurring pain points and improvement opportunities.
  • Support the analysis of employee feedback and onboarding results.
  • Help translate feedback and findings into practical program improvements.
  • Promote employee voice throughout the onboarding experience.
  • Monitor the consistency and quality of the employee experience across locations and employee populations.


Reporting and Performance Measurement

  • Maintain accurate onboarding records, participant information and program documentation.
  • Develop and update onboarding dashboards, status reports and performance indicators.
  • Monitor measures
  • Prepare regular program updates covering accomplishments, upcoming milestones, challenges, risks and opportunities.
  • Identify trends and recommend improvements to program execution and employee outcomes.
  • Protect employee information and maintain appropriate confidentiality.


Continuous Improvement

  • Support the continuous improvement of the Global Operations onboarding methodology, content and tools.
  • Review feedback, performance data and lessons learned.
  • Benchmark onboarding and employee-experience practices.
  • Help standardize and simplify onboarding processes across Global Operations.
  • Support the development and testing of new templates, tools and digital solutions.
  • Coordinate updates to onboarding materials with content owners and subject-matter experts.
  • Document processes and standard work to improve program consistency and sustainability.


Employee Life Cycle Program Support

  • Support selected initiatives across the broader Employee Experience & Capability Life Cycle as priorities evolve.
  • Help connect onboarding with development, performance, career growth, internal mobility, knowledge transfer and succession activities.
  • Maintain life-cycle documentation, process maps, tools and program trackers.
  • Support employee-listening activities at important moments throughout the employee journey.
  • Coordinate cross-functional actions arising from employee-experience findings.
  • Contribute to the development of an integrated and consistent employee experience across Global Operations.

What do you need to be successful?

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business Administration, Education, Communications, Project Management or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Approximately three to five years of experience in program coordination, onboarding, employee experience, learning and development, Human Resources or project coordination.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple activities, schedules, stakeholders and deliverables.
  • Strong organizational, planning and follow-up skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with employees, managers and leaders at different organizational levels.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities within a complex and changing environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook and Teams.
  • Experience maintaining program records, trackers, dashboards or status reports.

This position is part of a French-speaking work environment, it requires a very good knowledge of English to read and understand, on a daily basis, documentation and technical terms that may emanate from international organizations, as well as to write and communicate in English with customers, suppliers or international colleagues.

What do we offer?

  • Pension and savings plan with employer contributions

  • Group insurance program

  • Opportunities for advancement (career progression)

  • Merit or recognition program

  • Health and wellness program, including virtual health care

  • Recreational and sports club

  • Nearby daycares

  • Transportation accessibility or public transit program and free parking

Working at Pratt & Whitney Canada

Our work and the quality of our products contribute to the success of our customers, who in turn save lives, support commerce, connect communities, and protect freedoms.

At Pratt & Whitney Canada, you have the opportunity to make a difference every day—just look up. Are you ready to go beyond?

title: RF Engineer II
description:
Seeking a talented and highly motivated RF Design Engineer who will contribute to the development of electronic radio-frequency systems for space vehicle applications.

The RF Engineer II will:

  • Design front-end RF signal-chain circuits and assemblies for space vehicle communication and signal analysis systems using filters, amplifiers, mixers, couplers, transmission lines, impedance matching networks, and related components
  • Contribute to the design of stable, low-phase noise oscillators and distribution networks
  • Complete design, analysis, and test assignments efficiently and on schedule
  • Perform assignments with a moderate amount of technical guidance from senior-level engineers
  • Contribute to engineering documentation according to SEAKR’s workflow
  • Support PCB layout engineers to ensure circuit boards will meet RF performance requirements
  • Verify design performance with systematic laboratory measurements of engineering models
  • Perform worst case RF circuit analysis following SEAKR procedures
  • Assist in troubleshooting questionable RF hardware identified during test
  • Collaborate with RF Engineering Group to improve hardware development processes
  • Create clear reports and deliver summary presentations to product and project leadership with minimal review
  • BSEE or equivalent university degree
  • Understanding of linear RF circuit theory, including planar transmission line structures and wave propagation
  • Understanding of mixer circuit basics and performance parameters
  • Understanding of oscillator and clock circuit basics and performance parameters
  • Understanding of RF circuit and signal characterization including the application of scattering parameter measurements
  • Understanding of printed circuit board fabrication and automated assembly processes
  • Skills in schematic capture (Siemens Xpedition tools preferred)
  • Skills in RF design and analysis using commercial EDA tools (Cadence/AWR Microwave Office or Keysight ADS preferred)
  • Experience with 3D EM field modeling and CAD tools (Ansys HFSS preferred)
  • Experience in RF component and circuit verification measurements using multi-GHz VNAs, Spectrum Analyzers, Vector Signal Analyzers, Vector Signal Sources, and/or Phase Noise Analyzers
  • Experience working in collaborative design where success depends on collective efforts
  • Experience in presenting briefings and design reviews to internal project teams
  • Understanding of sampling and signal processing in digital RF systems is a plus

Compensation: Base salary range is $90,000-120,000/year, depending on qualifications. SEAKR has very rich medical, dental and vision insurance plans, along with a generous 401(k) retirement plan. In addition to base salary, employees are eligible for a year-end bonus. SEAKR offers a variety of paid leave, such as vacation, sick, bereavement, and FMLA.

SEAKR is an Equal Opportunity Employer - All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

US Citizenship Required

Applications will be accepted until 9/2/26.

  • Drive decisions and clear, accurate communication across technical and business audiences.
  • Flex across the delivery lifecycle — planning, execution, cutover, Hypercare, and decommissioning — depending on where the program needs support.
  • Measure adoption and impact post-release (30/60/90-day check-ins) and feed insights back into the portfolio.
  • Adopt and reinforce FTMO best-practice playbooks (migration, cutover, testing, Hypercare, environment/process architecture) on every program, and contribute improvements back to the standard.
  • On programs that require it, own data migration end-to-end (strategy, plan, ETL cycles, reconciliation, and sign-off) as the single point of accountability, and build the reusable enterprise migration standard that future programs adopt.
  • When assigned, orchestrate end-to-end business architecture — sequencing environment readiness across the program lifecycle and designing the business process hand-offs across workstreams so the assembled program delivers a coherent end-to-end experience.

What You Need to Succeed

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; MBA a plus. PMP, PMI-ACP, PgMP, or CSM a plus.
  • 5+ years of program management experience in the software or related technology industry, across a range of program types.
  • Proven ability to ramp quickly on unfamiliar domains and deliver in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.
  • Experience managing teams of business and technical resources.
  • Fluency across Agile/Scrum, Waterfall, and hybrid methodologies, tailoring the approach for each program.
  • Experience with enterprise platforms (SAP S/4 HANA, Dynamics 365, or equivalent) a plus.

title: Account Director
description:
M+C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment is a full-service, earned-first agency operating across Consumer PR, Creator & Influencer, Partnership Marketing, Social, Experiential, Sport, and Entertainment.

We bring a deep bench of experience in lifestyle, sport, entertainment, fashion, technology, and CPG — with ambitions to expand into many other categories. Our approach blends always-on brand communications with big creative campaigns, from strategy and ideation through design, production, execution, and social amplification. Our PR, marketing, and influencer specialists work seamlessly with our in-house studio to deliver content across every medium, from film and photography to print, experiential, and beyond.

About the Role
The Account Director role requires an individual who is driven by the challenge of driving and executing communications ideas and strategies alongside your team. You are organized and passionate about your work. You demonstrate the ability to craft strategic communications campaigns and deliver innovative solutions for clients. You produce work of the highest possible standard while motivating a team and keeping clients satisfied. A passion for global culture, current trends, social and earned media is essential. We are looking for an individual who is tuned in and plugged in – in their professional and personal lives.

As an Account Director, you play a key role in the wider business and should have commercial awareness and an understanding of our business and objectives.

Key Responsibilities Include:

  • Be a dedicated, positive and enthusiastic team player and maintain strong working relationships

  • Ensure all accounts are being run impeccably by respective teams

  • Lead all junior and mid-level staff, mentoring, nurturing and delegating as needed

  • Provide a strong support for senior leadership, serving as a reliable, proactive, solution-oriented and valuable member of the team

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Lead strategic development for all client campaigns, from inception to implementation and execution

  • Demonstrate the ability to construct a clear, insightful and succinct strategy and brief to put your team members on the path to successful ideation

  • Display a very high-level of writing proficiency – this extends from succinct communication via email through to the creative capabilities of a press release and client plans

  • Assume full responsibility for all accounts, managing high-level discussions (i.e. strategy, budget, etc.) with clients as required

  • Cultivate strong relationships with clients and all client partners, serving as the day-to-day client lead across the account

  • Clearly display an ability to pre-empt and understand the way your core client/s think and strategize about their brands, enabling you to establish your leadership and problem-solving skills

  • Ensure the foundational requirements of account management are being followed by your team. This includes correct usage of budget trackers, status reports, briefing documents and other structural documentation that ensures account work is seamless, efficient, and organized

  • Lead the team in delegation of roles and next steps across all projects, overseeing timelines and ensuring all work is on track

  • As part of that delegation, display an ability to connect 1-1 with your junior team members, maintaining motivation and helping them to better development as problem solvers and creative thinkers

  • Stay abreast of all trends across culture, industry, and more, actively monitoring across all platforms and attending relevant industry events to reinvigorate the creative process and inform work

  • Demonstrate the importance to your team of sharing critical trend and market information, ensuring to synthesize information and deliver it to the client in a way that clearly shows the opportunity/benefit for their business

  • Provide exemplary client management, offering sound strategic, creative, and operational advice while demonstrating expert skill to build and maintain close client relationships

  • Be responsible for KPI creation for campaigns and ensuring the team reaches them

  • Oversee event management and execution, as well as talent negotiation, management and contracting

  • Manage staff press trips and experiences/activations

  • Develop and execute effective digital campaigns (within context of broader integrated campaigns)

  • Manage all client budgets including monitoring and reconciliation and fee negotiation, including a clear and efficient understanding of internal finance processes (I.E the timely completion of POs, tracking expenditure etc)

  • Showcase strong relationships with top-tier, high-level media and be able to leverage these to convert to impactful brand coverage

  • Pitch and securing consumer press coverage, and compile key messaging, media Q&A, and briefing docs for client spokespeople.

  • Work with top tier media to land news exclusives, and navigate challenging corporate communications situations including providing information on background and off-the-record.

  • Play a broader role within the agency, seeking and developing new business opportunities

  • Showcase an ability to ‘manage up’; working closely with SAD/VP/SVP team members to collaborate effectively on the overall management of the account and understanding what requires escalation to ensure progress

  • Experience working within an IAT setting and collaborating with agency partners across the marketing mix

  • Have a finger-on-the-pulse of internet culture, and willingness to learn about new social media sites and ways of communicating.

Experience Required:

  • 6-9 years of experience at an agency demonstrating leading and motivating a team and driving communications strategy, planning and execution

  • The ideal candidate will be a consumer PR generalist who has experience across major CPG, sprit/beverage and lifestyle brands

Great to Have:

  • Creator marketing, sports, and music experience is a plus

  • Fluency in Spanish is a plus

Compensation:

We offer a competitive salary, a comprehensive employer subsidized benefits package which includes group medical, dental and vision coverage, Health Savings Account, 401k retirement plan with annual company match, employee wellness, commuter benefits and cellular phone allowance, generous paid time off and employee volunteer day to encourage social responsibility giving time to the non-profit, community service or charity of your choice. Salary is dependent on experience but ranges from: $100,000– $110,000. All candidates must have the ability to work in the US; we are unable to sponsor any work visas for this role.

ABOUT M+C SAATCHI GROUP

M+C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment, NA as part of M+C Saatchi Group has pledged its commitment to create a company that values difference, with an inclusive culture. As part of this M+C Saatchi Group continues to be an Equal Opportunity Employer which does not and shall not discriminate, celebrates diversity and bases all hiring and promotion decisions solely on merit, without regard for any personal characteristics.
