title: Weighing Associate
description:
JOB PURPOSE

To provide weighing of items for sale and production, while ensuring that it is completed safely with high quality, and in a timely manner. The Weighing Associate will foster a working environment that is clean and tidy, fair, positive, and driven to continuously improve.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain a High Level of Safety:

  • Understand and foresee and report possible safety issues.
  • Abide by health and safety guidelines prescribed by governing bodies and the TRC Environmental Health and Safety Committee.
  • General housekeeping of work area.
  • Promote a safe working environment.
  • Work in a manner that does not jeopardize the safety of self or co-workers.
  • Work safely and follow company safety policy and procedures and completing regular quality product checks.
  • Adhere to the department 5S standards.

Receive and Retrieve Correct Chemical Compounds:

  • Retrieve chemical compounds from inventory for weighing and packaging.
  • Ensure all chemical compounds are returned and stored appropriately.
  • Inspect and verify product labelling before assigning storage locations.
  • Work safely and follow company safety policy and procedures and completing regular quality product checks.
  • Prioritize chemical products to be picked according to First in – First Out (FIFO).
  • Report any loss or missing items to the Finished Goods supervisor.
  • Maintain proper organization of storage areas and update the inventory database as required.
  • Communicate any potential issues to the Finished Goods team lead or supervisor.
  • Ensure that all incoming new products from the Warehouse or Quality teams get properly labelled and stored according to appropriate storage conditions.

Weigh and Verify Orders

  • Carefully and accurately weigh chemicals as required.
  • Use appropriate containers and follow weighing instructions.
  • Inspect and verify orders, and product labelling before final packaging.
  • Prioritize chemical products to be picked according to First in First Out (FIFO)
  • Report any loss or missing items to the Finished Goods supervisor.
  • Communicate any potential issues to the Finished Goods team lead or supervisor.

Perform Other Duties

  • Perform other duties and complete additional projects as assigned.
  • Minimum College diploma

Competencies

  • 1-2 years of working experience in a similar field is preferred.
  • Good planning & organizing skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills.
  • Previously worked with a balance with good knowledge of measuring units.
  • Good command of the English language.
  • Excellent team player.
  • Self-starter, task oriented with ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.
  • Independently solves problems within his/her scope.

Physical & Working Conditions

  • Working closely with chemical compounds including ones that are potentially toxic or classified as Dangerous Goods and be treated accordingly.
  • Required to wear Personal Protective Equipment while handling chemicals such as a respirator which requires fit testing. Clean shaving is required to be compliant with this PPE requirement.
  • Must be available for: A second shift (9:30 am to 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday)
  • Shift may change to a different shift depending on business needs.

Pay range for this role is:

Minimum: CAD $42,000/ yearly

Maximum: CAD $45,000/ yearly

The salary range provided covers the minimum and maximum amounts projected for this role. The base salary will be influenced by factors like experience, skills, and location.

What we offer (Canada based-employees)

  • Competitive compensation
  • Comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits for employees and dependents
  • RRSP with matching employer contribution
  • Group retirement plan
  • PTO and Personal Care Days
  • Professional development and extended growth opportunities across the TRC and LGC networks
  • Subsidized corporate gym membership with GoodLife Fitness and store and restaurant discounts
  • Cheer Program where employees are recognized for outstanding work

LGC is a leading, global life science tools company, providing mission-critical components and solutions into high-growth application areas across the human healthcare and applied market segments. Its high-quality product portfolio is comprised of mission-critical tools for genomic analysis and for quality assurance applications, which are typically embedded and recurring within our customers’ products and workflows and are valued for their performance, quality, and range.

title: Senior Associate ICFR (AMEA)
description:
Securitas Group

Securitas is a world-leading safety and security solutions partner that helps make your world a safer place. By leveraging technology in partnership with our clients, we offer a broad portfolio of value-enhancing services and solutions integrated across the security value chain – from on-site services to advanced monitoring, comprehensive risk prediction and advisory services.

With around 322 000 employees in 44 markets, our innovative, holistic approach with local and global expertise makes us a trusted business partner to many of the world’s best-known companies. Benefitting from almost nine decades of deep experience and guided by our values of integrity, vigilance, and helpfulness, we create sustainable value by helping our clients optimize their operations and protect what matters most - their people and assets.

About the Role

Securitas is seeking a highly motivated ICFR Associate to support the Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR) program across 12 countries within the AMEA region. The role will be responsible for assessing and monitoring financial controls, supporting risk assessments, driving remediation activities, and leveraging technology and AI-enabled analytics to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of ICFR related activities.

This position offers an opportunity to work in a complex, multicultural environment while contributing to the strengthening of financial governance, compliance, and risk management across the region.

Responsibilities

ICFR Program Execution & Compliance

  • Conduct ICFR testing to evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of group controls processes (Purchase to pay, Sales to cash, FSCP, Payroll, treasury, fixed assets, etc) across AMEA countries.

  • Perform walkthroughs, control testing, and documentation reviews.

  • Support management in identifying control gaps, root causes, and remediation plans.

  • Evaluate segregation of duties (SoD), authorization controls, and financial reporting risks.

Risk Assessment & Controls Monitoring

  • Perform financial reporting risk assessments and identify emerging control risks.

  • Analyze control deficiencies and provide recommendations for improvement.

  • Review balance sheet accounts for significant quarterly movement

Digitalization & Continuous Improvement

  • Utilize data analytics/ Power BI/ Microsoft Copilot, and AI-enabled tools to enhance control monitoring and testing efficiency.

  • Support automation, dashboard development, and digital transformation initiatives within the ICFR program.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and strengthen finance controls and processes.

Policies, SOPs & Process Reviews

  • Partner with countries’ finance teams to review, update, and enhance finance policies and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

  • Ensure alignment with Group requirements and best practices.

  • Conduct end-to-end process reviews to identify control gaps, inefficiencies, and assist countries in amending where improvement opportunities.

Requirements

  • 3-5 years of experience in ICFR / SOX compliance, Internal Audit, Risk Advisory, Financial Controls, External Audit

  • Experience working in multinational organizations or Big 4 firms is preferred. Exposure to multi-country or regional compliance environments is an advantage.

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, or related field.

  • CA/ACCA/CPA/CIA or equivalent professional qualification is an advantage.

  • Travels: Up to 25% travel within the AMEA region required.

Location:

Role is based in Securitas AMEA office in India, Gurugram.

What we offer

At Securitas we believe in doing the right thing and doing it well. For our customers and our employees. Our employees come from all walks of life and bring with them many talents and perspectives. We aim for diverse representation throughout the company, and we are committed to equal pay, safe working conditions, gender balance and an inclusive work environment with a wide range of skills and development opportunities.

If this sounds like the right next step in your professional career, don't hesitate and apply!
